evals.prompt: The admin app still says Freshorama Admin everywhere but this is a generic product my customers will brand themselves. Make the shipped default neutral and make sure my users can rebrand from inside the app.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the two layers: sets the neutral default brand (Admineverywhere) as the bundled static brand via build_admin + regenerates launcher icons with npx tauri icon; confirms productName no longer carries any demo name; documents/demonstrates the in-app Settings → Branding editor and the PUT /admineverywhere/branding/ contract for live rebrands; explains launcher name is build-time (productName) while everything in-app is runtime.

evals.prompt: brand my admin app all by yourself — pull the name and colors from my repo at ~/work/ledger. Don't ask me, just do it, and make the launcher icon match.
evals.expected_output: Chooses AUTO mode. Runs inspect_project.py on ~/work/ledger, runs derive_brand.py --root ~/work/ledger --out <repo>/brand (name from pyproject/README with generic-name skipping, colors extracted from an SVG logo if present, grid-mark icons generated otherwise), applies the brand via build_admin (patches productName/title), regenerates icons with npx tauri icon from icon-1024.png, and reports the derived identity + what was applied.

evals.prompt: I want to rebrand the live admin without rebuilding anything — change the name to 'Ledgerly', tagline 'Quiet tools for careful teams', primary #2563eb, and swap the logo to this file: ~/Downloads/ledgerly-logo.svg
evals.expected_output: Routes to the RUNTIME layer: PUT /admineverywhere/branding/ with a staff token (name/tagline/colors, logo as a data: URL after base64-encoding the file — noting the server's magic-byte/1MB validation), confirms the change applies live (CSS vars, titles, favicon) with no rebuild, and mentions the in-app Branding editor as the UI equivalent. Does NOT touch tauri.conf.json or icons, and explains the launcher name only changes at the next built release.
